Sets the space's recurring schedule from an RFC 5545 RRULE, a first start time (wall-clock time
in the space's timezone; it must exist and be unambiguous there) and a duration of 1–1440
minutes. Editing an active series keeps the same rule id and occurrence keys: future
occurrences that are still occurrences of the edited rule are kept (with the new duration;
rescheduled ones keep their own time) together with their exceptions, while occurrences that
no longer match are removed or cancelled and their exceptions dropped; past occurrences are
never touched. Occurrences within the scheduling horizon are created right away. Requires
permission to schedule conferences (owner and host; co-host by default) and v2 meetings enabled
for the account. Archived spaces cannot recur.

delete.summary: End the recurring series (past occurrences are preserved).
delete.description:
Ends the space's active recurrence: every future unstarted occurrence of the series, including
rescheduled ones, is removed or cancelled, while started or past occurrences and the recorded
exceptions are kept. Requires
permission to schedule conferences (owner and host; co-host by default). Succeeds with 204 even
when there is no active recurrence.

get.summary: List exceptions of the active series.
get.description:
Returns the cancelled or rescheduled occurrences recorded for the space's active recurrence,
ordered by original start time, each with the series timezone. Returns an empty list when there
is no active recurrence. The caller must be a signed-in owner or member of the space.

put.summary: Cancel or reschedule ONE future occurrence of the series.
put.description:
Works whether or not the occurrence has been materialized yet. Idempotent; applied by the
scheduler when the occurrence is generated (or immediately if it already exists).

400.description: VALIDATION_ERROR (not an occurrence, past, bad window)

get.summary: Registrations of a meeting space (organizer view).
get.description:
Returns up to 500 registrations of the space, newest first, including cancelled ones, with the
attendee details collected at registration. Admission tokens are never returned. Requires a
signed-in owner, host or co-host of the space and webinar mode enabled.

post.summary: Register for a webinar / town hall (public when the profile enables registration).
post.description:
Registers an attendee for the whole meeting series or, with `conferenceId`, a single occurrence,
and returns a one-time-visible admission token for joining as a viewer. No sign-in is needed; a
signed-in caller's account is linked to the registration. Which fields (email, organization,
custom fields) are required or accepted is set by the meeting profile. Repeating a request with
the same `idempotencyKey` returns 200 with the existing registration and no token. Returns
REGISTRATION_DISABLED (404) when registration is not available for the space and
REGISTRATION_CLOSED when the chosen occurrence has ended or been cancelled; rate-limited per
meeting space.

get.summary: One registration (organizer view).
get.description:
Returns one registration of the space with the attendee details collected at registration; the
admission token is never returned. Requires a signed-in owner, host or co-host of the space and
webinar mode enabled.

delete.summary: Cancel a registration (revokes its admission token).
delete.description:
Marks the registration CANCELLED and revokes its admission token so it can no longer be used to
join. Requires a signed-in owner, host or co-host of the space and webinar mode enabled.
Cancelling an already-cancelled registration returns it unchanged.

post.summary: End every Messaging client session of the caller (all devices).
post.description:
Asks the Messaging service to revoke every client session of the signed-in user's principal, on
all devices. No request body is used. Messaging's status and body are returned unchanged.
Requires a bearer user token whose revocation status could be checked and the Messaging
integration enabled.

post.summary: Issue a short-lived, device-bound Messaging client token (for the realtime gateway).
post.description:
Requests a short-lived Messaging client token bound to one of the signed-in user's devices, for
connecting to the Messaging realtime gateway. The JSON body is forwarded as-is to the Messaging
service acting as the caller's own principal, and Messaging's status and body are returned
unchanged; no service credential is ever returned. Requires a bearer user token whose revocation
status could be checked and the Messaging integration enabled.

post.summary: Register a device with its proof-of-possession KeyPackage.
post.description:
Completes registration of a Messaging device for the signed-in user. The JSON body, as defined
by the Messaging contract, is forwarded as-is to the Messaging service acting as the caller's
own principal, and Messaging's status and body are returned unchanged; no service credential is
ever returned. Requires a bearer user token whose revocation status could be checked and the
Messaging integration enabled.

post.summary: Start a device registration (the challenge the device signs with its own key).
post.description:
First step of registering a Messaging device for the signed-in user; complete it with
`POST /api/v2/messaging/devices`. The JSON body is forwarded as-is to the Messaging service,
acting as the caller's own Messaging principal (created on first use), and Messaging's status
and body are returned unchanged. Requires a bearer user token whose revocation status could be
checked (the call fails closed otherwise) and the Messaging integration enabled.

post.summary: Publish one-time KeyPackages of the caller's device.
post.description:
Uploads one-time KeyPackages for the given device of the signed-in user, so the device can be
added to conversations. The JSON body is forwarded as-is to the Messaging service acting as the
caller's own principal, and Messaging's status and body are returned unchanged. Requires a
bearer user token whose revocation status could be checked and the Messaging integration
enabled.

post.summary: Revoke one of the caller's devices.
post.description: Optional `reason`: USER_REQUESTED (default), LOST_OR_STOLEN, COMPROMISED or REPLACED.

get.summary: Colleagues (active members of the caller's organizations) the caller may message.
get.description:
Returns up to 200 people who are active members of the caller's verified organizations (the
caller excluded), sorted by name, optionally filtered by `q` (case-insensitive substring match
on the name). `principalId` is null for people who have not used Messaging yet; use
`POST /api/v2/messaging/directory/resolve` to obtain it. Returns an empty list when the caller
has no verified organization. Requires a bearer user token whose revocation status could be
checked and the Messaging integration enabled.

200.description: people: userId, displayName, principalId (null until first use)

post.summary: The Messaging principals of directory colleagues (so they can be added).
post.description:
Returns the Messaging principal id of each user in `userIds` (1–100), creating principals on
first use, so the client can add those people to a conversation. Every user must be an active
member of one of the caller's verified organizations and not the caller; otherwise the request
fails with NOT_FOUND, exactly as for an unknown user. Requires a bearer user token whose
revocation status could be checked and the Messaging integration enabled.

get.summary: The caller's Messaging principal and device binding scope.
get.description:
Returns the caller's Messaging principal and the scope ids its devices bind into every
encrypted message.

post.summary: Display names of the principals the caller can see (self and colleagues).
post.description:
Returns display names for up to 256 `principalIds`. Only the caller's own principal and those of
active members of the caller's verified organizations are named; any other id is left out of the
answer without an error. Requires a bearer user token whose revocation status could be checked
and the Messaging integration enabled.

get.summary: Relayed read (allowlisted path under `v1/`, e.g. `v1/conversations/{id}/messages`).
get.description:
Forwards an allowlisted GET of the Messaging client API (for example conversations, members,
messages, unread counts, MLS state, device welcomes or history transfers) to the Messaging
service, acting as the caller's own principal, which is never taken from the request. The path
must match the allowlist exactly, with lowercase canonical UUIDs; anything else returns
ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND and is not forwarded. Only the query keys allowed for that path are accepted
(at most 8 pairs). Messaging's status and JSON body are returned unchanged; requires a bearer
user token whose revocation status could be checked.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: An allowlisted Messaging customer path under v1/

post.summary: Relayed create / action (allowlisted path under `v1/`).
post.description:
Forwards an allowlisted POST of the Messaging client API (for example creating a conversation,
adding members, posting a message or MLS commit, claiming KeyPackages, attachment uploads and
grants, or history transfers) to the Messaging service, acting as the caller's own principal,
which is never taken from the request. The JSON body (at most 1 MiB; empty means `{}`) is
forwarded as-is, and an `Idempotency-Key` header is forwarded only where the operation accepts
one, such as creating a conversation. Paths outside the allowlist return ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND and
are not forwarded. Messaging's status and JSON body are returned unchanged.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: An allowlisted Messaging customer path under v1/

put.summary: Relayed replace (allowlisted path under `v1/`, e.g. a read cursor or sealed history).
put.description:
Forwards an allowlisted PUT of the Messaging client API (a conversation read cursor or the
sealed history of a history transfer) to the Messaging service, acting as the caller's own
principal, which is never taken from the request. The JSON body (at most 1 MiB; empty means
`{}`) is forwarded as-is. Paths outside the allowlist return ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND and are not
forwarded. Messaging's status and JSON body are returned unchanged.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: An allowlisted Messaging customer path under v1/

delete.summary: Relayed removal (allowlisted path under `v1/`, e.g. leaving a conversation).
delete.description:
Forwards an allowlisted DELETE of the Messaging client API (removing a conversation member,
including leaving, or deleting a message) to the Messaging service, acting as the caller's own
principal, which is never taken from the request. No body is sent. Paths outside the allowlist
return ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND and are not forwarded. Messaging's status and JSON body are returned
unchanged.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: An allowlisted Messaging customer path under v1/

patch.summary: Relayed partial update (allowlisted path under `v1/`, e.g. editing a MANAGED message).
patch.description:
Forwards an allowlisted PATCH of the Messaging client API (updating a conversation's
lifecycle, expiry, retention or display title, changing a member's role, or editing a
MANAGED message with its `expectedEditCount`) to the Messaging service, acting as the
caller's own principal, which is never taken from the request. The JSON body (at most
1 MiB; empty means `{}`) is forwarded as-is; Messaging enforces ownership, roles and
optimistic concurrency. Paths outside the allowlist return ENDPOINT_NOT_FOUND and are
not forwarded. Messaging's status and JSON body are returned unchanged.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: An allowlisted Messaging customer path under v1/

post.summary: Issue a short-lived MANAGED-realtime session-device token (no E2EE device needed).
post.description:
Blueprint Section 13 (ADR 0049 amendment A1): returns a Messaging client token bound to
a *session device* of the signed-in user. A session device is not an MLS device: it can
only open the realtime gateway and subscribe to MANAGED conversations; it cannot publish
KeyPackages, join MLS groups, receive PRIVATE_E2EE ciphertext, use device-direct REST
operations or count as an end-to-end encrypted device. It is bound to the caller's
account session: the token never outlives the presented access token, every renewal
re-verifies the session, and signing out (this session, everywhere, or a security
revocation) ends it. Send `sessionDeviceId` to renew the same session device (an open
connection then continues with `auth.refresh`). Answers FEATURE_DISABLED while
Messaging has session devices switched off.

post.summary: Accept an organization invitation.
post.description:
Joins the organization with the invitation's role. The signed-in account must have a verified
email equal to the invited address (the account's verified email is sent by the server, never
taken from the request). An expired invitation answers INVITE_EXPIRED; an unknown, used or
revoked token answers INVITATION_INVALID. Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations
Service is authoritative.

post.summary: Decline an organization invitation.
post.description:
Declines a PENDING invitation addressed to the signed-in user so it can no longer be accepted.
Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations Service is authoritative.

post.summary: Create a business organization (the caller becomes OWNER).
post.description:
Creates a first-party business organization in the Organizations Service with the signed-in
user as its OWNER (creation source SELF_SERVICE; at most 5 per user per 24 hours). This is the
CF Meet business organization, not a developer-platform API workspace. Send an
`Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe. Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations
Service is authoritative.

get.summary: Get a business organization.
get.description:
Returns the organization with its profile, member count and the caller's own membership
(`viewer`: role, status and capabilities). Organizations the caller does not belong to answer
ORGANIZATION_NOT_FOUND, exactly like unknown ones. Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the
Organizations Service is authoritative.

patch.summary: Update a business organization's name, slug or profile.
patch.description:
Changes the name, slug and profile fields given (an omitted profile field is unchanged and
`null` clears it). `expectedVersion` must be the organization's current `version`, otherwise
VERSION_CONFLICT. Requires the `organization.profile.write` capability (OWNER, ADMIN). Returns
FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations Service is authoritative.

post.summary: Archive a business organization (OWNER).
post.description:
Archives an organization its OWNERs suspended; archiving is final for members (only OWNERs can
still read it) and existing organization meetings lose organization access. Requires the
`organization.lifecycle.manage` capability (OWNER). Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the
Organizations Service is authoritative.

get.summary: An organization's audit history.
get.description:
Returns the organization's audit events, newest first (`before` = the `seq` of the oldest
event already seen; `limit` 1–200, default 50): who changed what, when, and through which
service. Requires the `organization.audit.read` capability (OWNER, ADMIN). Returns
FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations Service is authoritative.

parameters.name: before
parameters.description: Return events older than this sequence number

get.summary: List an organization's invitations.
get.description:
Returns the organization's invitations (masked invitee email, never a token), optionally
filtered by `status`. Requires the `organization.members.invite` capability. Returns
FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations Service is authoritative.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: PENDING, ACCEPTED, DECLINED, REVOKED or EXPIRED

post.summary: Invite someone to an organization by email.
post.description:
Creates a PENDING invitation for `email` with `role` and returns it with its one-time `token`
(shown only in this response; only the token's hash is stored). Only an account whose verified
email equals the invited address can accept it. Requires the `organization.members.invite`
capability (OWNER, ADMIN, MANAGER). Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe.
With `sendEmail: true` the invitation link is also emailed to the invitee when notification
email is enabled on the deployment (`emailDelivery` reports the outcome; an idempotent replay
re-issues the token and emails the new link). Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations
Service is authoritative.

post.summary: Revoke an organization invitation.
post.description:
Revokes a PENDING invitation so its token can no longer be accepted (idempotent: revoking a
revoked invitation succeeds). Requires the `organization.members.invite` capability. Returns
FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations Service is authoritative.

get.summary: List members (platform admins, organization OWNER/ADMIN).
get.description:
Returns every membership of the organization, whatever its status, oldest first. Allowed for
platform administrators and for active OWNER or ADMIN members of an active organization. Once
the Organizations Service is authoritative, the list comes from it (removed memberships are
omitted; members holding `organization.members.read` may list) and each item also carries
`organizationRole` and `version`.

post.summary: Leave an organization.
post.description:
Ends the signed-in user's own membership. The last OWNER cannot leave (LAST_OWNER): transfer
ownership first. Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations Service is authoritative.

put.summary: Add or change a membership (platform admins, organization OWNER/ADMIN within limits).
put.description:
Creates or updates the user's role and status in the organization; status REMOVED ends an
existing membership. Platform administrators and OWNERs may set any role, while ADMINs may only
manage MEMBER memberships. Except for platform administrators, callers cannot change their own
membership. Once the Organizations Service is authoritative, an existing member's change is
relayed to it (its role rules apply) and a user who is not yet a member gets
`409 INVITATION_REQUIRED`: new members join by invitation.

patch.summary: Change a member's role or status.
patch.description:
Changes the role (OWNER, ADMIN, MANAGER, MEMBER, GUEST) or status (ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, REMOVED)
of one membership. The path's member segment is the membership `id` from the member list.
`expectedVersion` must be the membership's current `version`. The Organizations Service
enforces the role rules: OWNERs manage anyone, ADMINs manage MANAGER, MEMBER and GUEST
memberships, nobody raises their own role, and the last OWNER cannot be removed or demoted
(LAST_OWNER). Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations Service is authoritative.

parameters.name: userId
parameters.description: Membership id (the `id` of a member list item)

post.summary: Transfer organization ownership.
post.description:
Atomically makes the membership `toMembershipId` an OWNER and the calling OWNER an ADMIN.
`expectedVersion` must be the organization's current `version`. Requires the
`organization.ownership.transfer` capability (OWNER). Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the
Organizations Service is authoritative.

get.summary: An organization's technical provisioning state.
get.description:
Returns the truthful provisioning state of the organization's technical scope (NOT_REQUIRED,
PENDING, IN_PROGRESS, READY or FAILED), the current step and, on failure, the failure class.
Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations Service is authoritative.

post.summary: Reactivate a business organization (OWNER).
post.description:
Reactivates an organization its OWNERs suspended (a suspension imposed by an operator can only
be lifted by an operator). Requires the `organization.lifecycle.manage` capability (OWNER).
Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the Organizations Service is authoritative.

post.summary: Suspend a business organization (OWNER).
post.description:
Suspends an ACTIVE organization: no member keeps any capability except that OWNERs can still
read it, so organization meetings, invitations and colleague lists stop. Requires the
`organization.lifecycle.manage` capability (OWNER). Returns FEATURE_DISABLED until the
Organizations Service is authoritative.

get.summary: Resolve any supported meeting identifier to the canonical space and conference.
get.description:
Accepts a v2 space id, v2 meeting code, legacy meeting id or legacy meeting code and returns the
matching space, its canonical conference (the LIVE one, else the next upcoming one, else the
latest) and `matchedBy` (V2_ID, V2_CODE, LEGACY_ID or LEGACY_CODE). Authentication is optional.
Resolving does not grant access: callers who cannot manage the space get the summary view only.
Unknown identifiers return MEETING_NOT_FOUND.

tags.name: Chat
tags.description:
In-meeting chat with hybrid real-time architecture.

## Architecture
- **LiveKit Data Channels**: Real-time message delivery via `publishData()` and `RoomEvent.DataReceived`
- **REST API**: Message persistence and history loading for late joiners

## Flow
1. **Send**: POST /chat (persist) → LiveKit publishData() (broadcast)
2. **Receive**: Listen to RoomEvent.DataReceived for instant delivery
3. **Late Join**: GET /chat to load message history

## Notes
- Messages are **volatile** - automatically deleted when meeting ends
- Only participants with 'joined' status can send/receive messages

tags.name: Users
tags.description:
User profile management and account operations.

## Endpoints
- **GET /users/me**: Get current user profile
- **PATCH /users/me**: Update profile (username only)
- **POST /users/me/deactivate**: Deactivate account (soft delete)

## Notes
- All endpoints require JWT authentication
- Deactivated users are blocked by auth middleware
- Deactivation immediately invalidates all tokens

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description:
Webhook management for event notifications.

## Events
- `meeting_start`: Triggered when a meeting begins
- `meeting_end`: Triggered when a meeting ends
- `participant_join`: Triggered when a participant joins
- `participant_leave`: Triggered when a participant leaves

## Security
- Each webhook has a unique secret for payload signing
- Secret is only shown once on creation
- Payloads are signed using HMAC-SHA256

## Notes
- Webhooks are user-scoped
- Delivery is async and failure-tolerant

tags.description: Waiting is a participant admission state. Access policy is always evaluated first.

tags.name: Organizations (v2)
tags.description: First-party CF Meet business organizations (not developer-platform API workspaces) and the organization membership used by ORGANIZATION_ONLY access. Membership is resolved server-side; clients can never assert it. Blueprint Section 4: once the Organizations Service is authoritative, these routes relay to it with the signed-in user as the verified acting user (create, profile, members, invitations, ownership transfer, lifecycle, audit, provisioning); until then the first-party routes answer FEATURE_DISABLED and the legacy directory routes are unchanged.

tags.name: Compatibility (v2)
tags.description: Legacy → v2 migration evidence and shadow comparison (platform administrators).

tags.name: Recordings (v2)
tags.description: Part G: composite recording through the provider egress. REQUESTED → RECORDING only on provider evidence; STOPPING → PROCESSING → READY only after provider finalization and storage verification (size + checksum). One active composite recording per conference.

tags.name: Artifacts (v2)
tags.description: Part G: recordings, transcripts and generated reports. Access is authorized per request and delivered as a short-lived signed URL; storage keys and provider ids are never exposed. Retention and deletion are confirmed against storage.

tags.name: Consent (v2)
tags.description: Part G: independent consent per processing type (recording, transcription, intelligence, data sharing), explicit or notice mode per meeting profile, and withdrawal semantics.

tags.name: Transcription (v2)
tags.description: Part G: provider-neutral transcription jobs, idempotent segment ingestion, WebVTT export and translation. Disabled unless a provider is configured and the profile permits it.

tags.name: Intelligence (v2)
tags.description: Part G: bounded intelligence requests over READY transcripts, gated by profile, consent and processing location. Production summarization is not part of this release.

tags.name: Profiles (v2)
tags.description: Part H: meeting profiles (STANDARD, WEBINAR, TOWN_HALL, HIGH_SECURITY, HEALTHCARE) resolved base → type → security → organization → space → conference with hard ceilings.

tags.name: Registrations (v2)
tags.description: Part H: webinar / town-hall registration with policy-approved fields and one-time admission tokens.

tags.name: Backstage (v2)
tags.description: Part H: isolated backstage media room for presenters and hosts.

tags.name: Quality (v2)
tags.description: Part I: bounded participant quality samples (technical metrics only) and scoped conference quality for hosts.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description:
Administrative endpoints for system management.

## Access
- All endpoints require admin role
- Role check is performed in each handler

## Endpoints
- **GET /admin/users**: List all users with pagination and filters
- **PATCH /admin/users/:id**: Update user role or status
- **GET /admin/meetings**: List all meetings with pagination and filters
- **GET /admin/logs**: List session logs with pagination and filters

## Notes
- Admins cannot change their own role
- Most operations are read-only
